document_summary: A Morgan Lewis LawFlash (Aug. 21, 2026) summarizing municipal algorithmic rent-pricing ordinances and follow-on litigation; the in-scope jurisdictions are San Francisco, San Diego, Berkeley, Santa Ana, Jersey City and Hoboken.

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy. Tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation, per unit per month
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords using qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information.
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance prohibits landlords from using qualifying algorithmic devices that calculate nonpublic competitor information to advise on rent or occupancy.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source (law firm alert). Effective date is given only as 'October 2024' in the summary table. Penalty cap (up to $1,000 per violation, each unit-month a separate violation) is in the source but is not the key value. Source cites subsections (b) and (d).

rules.title: San Diego ban on algorithmic rent-setting
rules.requirement: San Diego prohibits landlords from using algorithmic rent-setting tools that rely on competitor data, similar to the San Francisco ban. Tenants may sue for damages and injunctive relief.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices; private remedy of up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or rental property owners using the covered algorithmic rent-setting products; each month and affected rental property may be a separate violation.
rules.quoted_span: Similar prohibition and private remedy of up to $1,000 per violation; now at issue in _Keller v. UDR Inc.,_ (S.D. Cal.).
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source. Effective date is given only as 'June 2025' in the summary table. 'Similar' refers to the San Francisco row above it in the table.

rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Berkeley prohibits landlords from using coordinated pricing algorithms for rents. Violations can recur per unit per month and carry private remedies.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits coordinated pricing algorithms; recurring unit/month violations and private remedies
rules.conflict_note: Open question: two published effective dates. This alert says January 2026; the ordinance text reportedly says 1 March 2026. The ordinance text is not found in this capture.
rules.extraction_notes: Effective date taken from this law-firm alert ('effective January 2026'). RealPage v. City of Berkeley was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice on Jan. 14, 2026, per the source.

rules.title: Santa Ana Ordinance NS-3090 on automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: Prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing. Tenants may bring private claims.
rules.key_value: Ban on automated rent price-fixing; up to $1,000 per violation and per month
rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source. Effective date 'April 2, 2026' is stated in the summary table. Codification in the Santa Ana Municipal Code is not given.

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ordinance is enforced both publicly and privately.
rules.key_value: Ban on landlord use of algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.interaction: New Jersey's FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once it takes effect. This document does not address it.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.conflict_note: Possible preemption by the New Jersey FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) once effective. Not found in this capture.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source. Effective date is given only as 'June 2025' in the summary table. The $2,000 per day fine is not the key value.

rules.title: Hoboken ban on algorithmic rent coordination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy.
rules.key_value: Ban on software/algorithm/data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy
rules.interaction: New Jersey's FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once it takes effect. This document does not address it.
rules.quoted_span: Prohibits landlords from using software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy.
rules.conflict_note: Possible preemption by the New Jersey FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c.43) once effective. Not found in this capture.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source. Effective date is given only as 'July 2025' in the summary table. The citation is given in the source as 'ch. 158-2'.
